*Proof.* These operators are limit point at both end points *r* = 0, and *r* = *∞*. Indeed, any solution <u>3</u> *−* <u>1</u> of *Lf* = 0 or *Ljf* = 0 is asymptotic to a linear combination of *r²,r*2as *r →* 0+, so no boundary condition is needed at *r* = 0. The other endpoint *r* = *∞* is standard, see [53, Theorem X.8]. The claim about essential self-adjointness is [53, Theorem X.7]. See [30, Section 4] for the Bessel operator *L₀* and its domain. The Kato-Rellich theorem applies to *L,L₁,L₂*, which are relatively bounded perturbations of *L₀*, see [17, Section 1.4] (in fact, these operators are perturbations of *L₀* by bounded operators). The Weyl criterium, see [54, Theorem XIII.14], implies that specess(*L₀*) = specess(*L₁*) = [0*, ∞*). If *λ ∈* spec(*L₁*) for some *λ <* 0, then there exists a ground state of negative <u>3</u> energy, i.e., *L₁ϕ* = *λ₀ϕ* for some *λ₀ <* 0 and *ϕ ∈D* with *ϕ >* 0 (in fact, *ϕ* is smooth and *ϕ*(*r*) *∼ cr²* as *r →* 0+ for some constant *c*). Let *χ*(*r*) = 1 for 0 *≤ r ≤* 1, *χ ∈ C* *∞* ([0*, ∞*)) with compact support, and set *χb*(*r*) = *χ*(*r/b*) with *b ≥* 1. Then <u>1 1</u> *⟨L₁ϕ,χb*(*r*)*r² ρ₁⟩* = *λ₀⟨ϕ,χb*(*r*)*r² ρ₁⟩*

Integrating by parts on the left-hand side and sending *b → ∞* now leads to a contradiction be- <u>1</u> cause of the vanishing *L₁*(*r² ρ₁*) = 0. Hence *L₁ >* 0 as stated (note that *L₁* cannot have a zero energy eigenfunction because the unique 0-energy solution is not in *X₀*). Pure a.c. spectrum is a consequence of the construction of the Weyl, Titchmarsh *m*-function for these operators, see [30,40]. The essential spectrum of *L₂* follows from the Weyl criterium as before. Since *L₂* = *L₁* + 2*ρ²*1*>* 0, we conclude that the discrete spectrum of *L₂* – if it exists – is strictly positive. □
